Print pilot plans and confidence rectangles

Source: R/print_summary.R
print.cmr_pilot_plan.Rd

Compact display methods for pilot-planning objects and for the confidence rectangles returned by the rectangle_*() constructors. They show the headline entries. The full object remains an ordinary list.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'cmr_pilot_plan'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'cmr_pilot_viability_band'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'cmr_binary_rectangle'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'cmr_unbounded_rectangle'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'cmr_multiarm_rectangle'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'cmr_stratified_rectangle'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'cmr_multiple_outcomes_rectangle'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A cmr_pilot_plan, cmr_pilot_viability_band, or confidence rectangle object.

...

Reserved for future extensions.

Value

The original object, invisibly.

See also

Other pilot planning: activation_threshold_bounded(), break_even_pilot_share(), pilot_plan(), pilot_viability_band()

Other rectangle helpers: binary_rectangle_corners(), cmr_multiarm_from_rectangle(), cmr_stratified_from_rectangle(), cmr_unbounded_from_rectangle(), folded_binomial_pmf(), multiarm_variance_objective(), rectangle_bernoulli_binary(), rectangle_bounded_two_arm(), rectangle_multiarm(), rectangle_multiple_outcomes(), rectangle_proxy(), rectangle_stratified(), rectangle_unbounded(), stratified_variance_objective(), variance_bounds_bernoulli_exact(), variance_bounds_maurer_pontil(), variance_bounds_unbounded_mom()

Examples

cmr_plan(n = 3000, sigma1 = 0.18, sigma0 = 0.28, desired_pilot = 120)
#> <cmr_pilot_plan>
#>   n: 3000
#>   method: bounded, accounting: design_only
#>   viability band: 72 to 134 (even sizes)
#>   suggested_pilot: 72
#>   default_two_thirds_power: 210 (above_break_even_cap)
#>   desired_pilot: 120 (inside_viability_band)

d <- rep(c(1, 0), each = 6)
y <- c(1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1)
rectangle_two_arm(y, d)
#> <cmr_binary_rectangle>
#>   rectangle: v_l1=0.02915, v_u1=0.25, v_l0=0.02915, v_u0=0.25
#>   method: bernoulli
#>   n: 12
#>   joint_error_bound: 0.05
